title: The 'No More White Bands for Roy' headline
summary: A headline misrepresented his comment about having his own group, leading to attacks, with Zoot Sims and Phil Brown in the band.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah! And there was a difference, you know? Then the biggest goof of all, when he said, "Well, do you think you might go back with Gene or Benny Goodman or Artie Shaw?" and I said, "Now I have my own group." What's wrong

Yeah. Then he opened up with "No More White Bands For Roy." And that did it. That's what did it, you know. They didn't even read the thing good. But "No More White Bands For Roy" really did it. Because they thought I was putting the White race down, you know? And it didn't have nothin' to do with that at all.
It must have been '51, because I came back in '51.
Yeah, that was a way to make headlines.

They sure made it! Boy, did I get a lot of flak from that. You know, I had Zoot working with me. We went to Philadelphia, and people come and say, "What are you doing with him?" I had another White player, a drummer, Paul Brown. Did you ever hear of him?
I don't know where he's from, really. He could be from Philadelphia. But I had him playing drums

with me... Maybe it was Phil Brown. And then they come and said, "Well, what are doing with these White cats here? I thought you didn't like White people." And it got really so goddamn ridiculous. And I ended up being a Communist, too, on top of that, you know! Finally, I said, "Look, why don't you let Zoot be the leader. I'm going back to New York. I can't stand this shit no more." All for nothing -- "No More White Bands For Roy."

I could have really unloaded on him, man, but I didn't, about he wanted to do away with himself. And I got that axe hanging over him. If he ever really unloads on me again, I'm gonna really open up the floodgates on him! But I don't dig hurtin' the cat, you know. Oh, what shit. What can you do?
